sections.heading: What’s Inside the Victoria Rig Pack — 10 Rigs Total
sections.text: • 3 × Gummy & School Shark Rigs Gummy & School Shark Rig – 110lb Black Coated Wire / 8/0 Circle Hook Heavy-Duty Castable Gummy Shark Rig – 200lb Stainless Steel Wire / 8/0 Circle Hook • 2 × Snapper & Bay Paternoster Rigs 80lb Snapper Flasher Double Paternoster Rig – Twin 10/0 Sport Circle Hooks 60lb Kingfish & Snapper Twisted Flasher Paternoster Rig – Twin 6/0 Recurve Circle Hooks • 2 × Surf Casting Rigs — Tailor & Salmon Tailor & Surf Fishing Rig – Twin 4/0 Ganged Hooks / Sliding Sinker • 2 × Bream & Whiting Rigs 40lb Everyday Twisted Paternoster Rig – Twin 1/0 Beak Hooks • 1 × All-Round Bay, Beach & Inshore Rig All Species Fishing Rig – Adjustable Sliding Stinger Hook Rig quantities are weighted towards the styles that see the most consistent use in Victorian conditions. Victoria’s fishing is heavily influenced by tides, swell, current and water temperature. This pack focuses on rigs that: Perform reliably in southern surf and wash conditions Handle bay and inshore snapper fishing Provide castable options for gummy and school sharks Transition easily between beach, pier, rock and boat fishing Cover everything from whiting and bream through to sharks and larger bottom species These are practical rigs that Victorian customers regularly order and rely on.

sections.heading: Typical Victorian Target Species
sections.text: The rigs in this pack are commonly used to target: Gummy sharks School sharks Snapper, including pinkies Australian salmon Tailor King George whiting Mulloway Bream Flathead Trevally Kingfish Species availability varies by season and location, but this pack provides a versatile selection that remains useful throughout the year. Victorian conditions can change quickly. Keep a mixture of lighter bay and estuary rigs and heavier surf or bottom rigs ready—being able to change rigs quickly can often matter more than changing locations. Rinse rigs with fresh water after saltwater use Allow rigs to dry completely before storage Check wire, leaders, knots, swivels and hooks after gummy or shark captures Store rigs dry and separated to reduce tangles and corrosion Match your sinker weight to the surf, depth and current without exceeding your rod’s rating Replace any leader or wire showing kinks, abrasion or damage Well-maintained rigs last longer and fish more reliably.

sections.heading: Important WA Fishing Rules
sections.text: Western Australian fishing rules vary by bioregion, species, season and fishing method. When targeting demersal scalefish in the West Coast Bioregion, fishos may use a maximum of one bait or lure on each line . Any double-hook paternoster rig must therefore be converted to a genuine single-hook setup before being used for those species. The hooks on the included paternoster rigs can be unlooped and removed when a single-hook setup is required. Purpose-built WA-Compliant Single-Arm Twisted Paternoster Rig Blanks are also available. sections.heading: Western Australia Pro Tip
sections.text: In strong WA current, don’t automatically use the heaviest sinker available. Start lighter and increase the weight only when needed. A rig that moves slightly with the current can sometimes attract more bites than one pinned firmly to the bottom.

sections.heading: When the Reef Hits Back, These Rigs Hit Harder
sections.text: Born from years of testing on one of the toughest reef systems in Australia, the Swains Slayer Series™ is built for anglers who demand more than just “standard rigs.” Each design has been trialed and proven on our annual Swains Reef expeditions, where tooth, coral, and chaos punish anything unprepared. These rigs survived — and thrived — delivering fish after fish when lesser gear failed. These rigs were developed from real trips to Swains Reef — see Field Notes from Swains for what the reef taught us → On this page you’ll find every rig in the series, along with guidance on how to fish it, what species it targets, the baits that work best, and pro tips straight from the reef. Whether you’re chasing coral trout, red emperor, snapper, or pelagics, these rigs give you the edge. These rigs were designed as a specialised reef system based on real Swains Reef fishing conditions. While they’re built for demanding coral environments, the same designs perform strongly on reefs, rubble patches and offshore structure right around Australia. Scanning from your rig packet? Scroll down for bait recommendations, target species and setup tips for each rig in the Swains Slayer Series. Want to see where these rigs sit within the wider Australian fishing rig system? Start with the Australian Fishing Rig Decision Guide → These rigs are built specifically for heavy reef structure like the Swains. If you're interested in how reef rigs differ from surf and estuary setups across Australia, learn more here → Explore the full lineup of Swains Slayer Rigs—each hand tied with premium gear in Australia—then scroll down for rig-by-rig breakdowns, pro tips, and maintenance advice.” For more general-purpose rig combinations used across different Australian states and conditions, see our State Fishing Rig Packs here →

sections.heading: FLOATING MACKEREL RIG (RIG 282)
sections.text: A purpose-built drift fishing rig armed with three ganged 8/0 hooks a flexible 80lb black coated stainless steel wire tied to a long heavy-duty 80lb monofilament leader. Designed for presenting whole or slab baits naturally while drifting or anchored over reefs, rubble, or drop-offs. The rig allows big baits to sit straight, perfect for targeting aggressive, toothey reef and pelagic species. Best For: Fishing in 10m–60m depths while drifting or anchored. Works well in moderate currents. Targets: Spanish Mackerel, Coral trout, Red emperor, Snapper, Cobia, Trevally and other hard-hitting predators. Recommended Baits: Whole pilchards, strip baits, whole squid, small reef fish. This rig is tied with a wire trace and a long 3m 80lb mono leader tied to a swivel. This gives you enough length to have the option to cut of the swivel and attach the leader directly to your mainline to make it easier for casting if you prefer. Keep the drift speed slow for a natural presentation. Rig baits straight on the gang for maximum hook exposure. Add a light burley trail to draw fish into your drift. Great when prospecting new ground — as it covers large areas of water and finds fish fast.

sections.heading: Drift Assassin II™
sections.text: A variation of the classic Drift Assassin™, fitted with two ganged 8/0 hooks instead of three. This design is ideal for anglers who prefer slightly smaller baits while still maintaining the strength and natural presentation of a gang rig. Best For: Drift fishing in 1 0m–30m depths , especially when fish are fussy or baitfish are smaller. Targets: Snapper, coral trout, spangled emperor, trevally, mackerel, and other mid-to-large predators. Recommended Baits: Whole pilchards, garfish, strip baits, squid heads. This rig is tied with a long 3m 80lb leader tied to a swivel. This gives you enough length to have the option to cut of the swivel and attach the leader directly to your mainline to make it easier for casting if you prefer. Great option when fish are biting shy and won’t take a larger presentation. Works well with slightly lighter drags to let fish swallow before the circle hook sets. Keep bait streamlined to maintain a natural drift.

sections.heading: REEF REAPER RIG (RIG 284)
sections.text: A rugged all-round reef rig designed to punch baits deep into heavy structure and pull big fish out. Built on flexible yet tough 80lb coated wire leader, this rig can take the punishment of coral ledges, bommies, and reef edges where the nastiest predators live. Best For: Working reefs, ledges, and drop-offs in 20–60m depths. Perfect when fishing anchored or lightly drifting over gnarly reef terrain. Targets: Coral trout, red emperor, cod, sweetlip, tuskfish, and other reef bruisers. Recommended Baits: Whole squid, hardy fillets, mullet strips, and flesh baits that can handle pecks from pickers. Drop baits tight against structure — that’s where the trophies lurk. Use heavier sinkers to get down fast before pickers strip your bait. Check leaders often; reef abrasion is unforgiving. Strike hard and turn fish quick, this rig can definitely handle it! or risk losing them in the reef.

sections.heading: DEPTH CHARGER RIG (RIG 290)
sections.text: A heavy-duty deep drop running rig armed with a size 10 ball sinker fixed into the build, paired with a luminous bead and fish-eye attractors. Finished with a single 8/0 circle hook on 100lb mono, this rig punches baits down fast to the strike zone in 20–60m depths. Best For: Bottom fishing where getting baits down quickly is critical — reefs, ledges, and deep rubble patches. Targets: Red emperor, nannygai, cod, coral trout, snapper, and other reef bruisers. Recommended Baits: Whole squid, fish fillets, flesh strips, or hardy baits that hold in current. This 100lb rig is tied with a long 2m 80lb leader tied to a swivel. This gives you enough length to have the option to cut of the swivel and attach the leader directly to your mainline to make it easier for casting if you prefer. (The long leader assists in safely pulling your catch into the boat, without handling your 'skin cutting' braid.) Drop straight down and hold position for best results. The luminous bead works best at dawn, dusk, and deeper water. When fishing at night, shine your torch on the beads before you drop for extra attractant Use fresh strip baits to resist pickers and tempt big fish. (If you use soft baits like pilchards, you'll be constantly winding back up n have arms like Popeye before you know it!)

sections.heading: DEPTH CHARGER XL (RIG 289)
sections.text: The big-bait upgrade of the Depth Charger™, featuring a double ganged 8/0 beak hook system . Built for larger slab or whole fish baits, it keeps presentations secure and straight when targeting true reef monsters. Built in size 10 sinker and beads as per the Original Depth Charger rig above. Best For: Deep dropping with big slab baits in 20–60m depths. Targets: XL coral trout, red emperor, cod, mackerel, and other oversized reef predators. Recommended Baits: Whole mullet, tailor, slimy mackerel, or large strip baits. This 100lb rig is tied with a long 2m 80lb leader tied to a swivel. This gives you enough length to have the option to cut of the swivel and attach the leader directly to your mainline to make it easier for casting if you prefer. (The long leader assists in safely pulling your catch into the boat, without handling your 'skin cutting' braid.) Drop big baits near structure — perfect for “one bite, one fish” encounters. Use strong drags and be ready to turn fish immediately. (Big Reds hit like a freight train and head straight for the reef, fight them hard from the start and get them up before the taxman get them!) Ideal for trophy hunting when size matters over numbers.

sections.heading: CORAL TROUT CRUSHER RIG (RIG 285)
sections.text: A specialised single-dropper paternoster with a realistic artificial crab lure positioned near the sinker. Proven deadly on coral trout, this rig entices aggressive strikes when bounced along reef edges and drop-offs. Best For: Fishing tight to reef structure in 15–40m depths . Targets: Coral trout primarily, but also cod, redthroat, spangled emperor and other reef species. Recommended Baits: You can use the crab lure alone; however, we seem to get the best results when we add small amounts of flesh bait or squid for added scent. Drop straight into reef ledges and lift slowly to imitate a fleeing crab. Short, sharp rod lifts trigger aggressive reaction bites. Always be ready — trout hit hard and head straight for cover.

sections.heading: TWISTED TWIN-STRIKE PATERNOSTER RIG (RIG 286)
sections.text: Twisted paternoster rigs are one of the most reliable reef setups used across Australia. Learn how they work and why they’re so effective here → A rugged two-dropper paternoster made from 80lb mono with red luminous beads and 8/0 beak hooks. The perfected dropper placement delivers maximum hook-up rates after years of trial and refinement. A great all round reef rig, based on one of the most popular rigs on the market. Best For: Versatile reef fishing in 20–70m depths with bait kept just off the bottom. Targets: Snapper, red emperor, sweetlip, tuskfish, coral trout, and more. Recommended Baits: Squid strips, pilchards, fish fillets, or cut baits. Drop straight down over reef edges or rubble. Use different baits on each dropper to find what fish prefer. The twisted dropper design reduces tangles and improves bait presentation.

sections.heading: BOTTOM BASHING PATERNOSTER FLASHER RIG (RIG 293)
sections.text: A classic paternoster rig fitted with luminous beads and flash material around the hooks, imitating small baitfish. Its tough design and eye-catching appeal make it effective across a wide variety of reef species. Best For: Bottom fishing in 20–60m depths , especially when fish need extra attraction. Targets: Coral trout, snapper, trevally, emperor, cod, and other common reef dwellers. Recommended Baits: Strip baits, Pilchards, squid strips, prawns — you can fish it bare to mimic tiny baitfish but we have found the additional scent when adding bait to be extremely productive Excellent choice when fish are shy — the flash draws them in. Works as both a baited rig and a bare “teaser” for opportunistic strikes. Ideal as a go-to when other rigs go quiet.

sections.heading: SKIRTED ASSASSIN RIG (RIG 291)
sections.text: A running rig armed with a 7/0 circle hook cloaked in a colourful silicone skirt and buoyed by a pompano float with lumo bead. The smaller size 7 ball sinker allows a natural drift down, perfect for fishing in depths up to 30m. Best For: Targeting mid-depth reefs and rubble patches with a lively, buoyant presentation. Targets: Snapper, redthroat, spangled emperor, coral trout, cod, and many more. Recommended Baits: Whole pilchards, strip baits, or squid strips tipped inside the skirt. The skirt adds movement and colour to draw fish in. Perfect for lightly weighted bait fishing in shallower reefs. Cast up-current and let the bait waft naturally into the strike zone.

sections.heading: SILENT SLIDING BALL SINKER RIG (RIG 292)
sections.text: Running sinker/fish finder rigs like this allow fish to take bait naturally without resistance. Learn how they’re used across different Australian fishing situations here → A simple but deadly running rig with a size 7 ball sinker sliding freely above an 80lb mono leader and a razor-sharp 8/0 beak hook. This stealth setup lets the fish take the bait without feeling resistance, making it perfect for fussy feeders. Designed for depths up to 20m, the Silent Assassin™ shines when anchored or slow drifting. Best For: Fishing anchored reefs or slow drifts where subtlety gets the bite. Targets: Spangled emperor, redthroat, coral trout, cod, and a wide range of reef species. Recommended Baits: Whole pilchards, squid strips, or small fish fillets for maximum effectiveness. Keep your sinker size light to maximise stealth and natural bait presentation. Ideal for overnight anchor sessions when fish are feeding cautiously. Match bait size to your target species for better hook-ups.

sections.heading: TWISTED PATERNOSTER BLANKS (RIGS 287 & 288)
sections.text: Heavy-duty twisted paternoster backbones, purpose-built for anglers who like options. Each blank comes pre-tied with a 165lb swivel, leaving the hook choice up to you. Perfect for quick changeovers when leaders get damaged or frayed, or when you want to swap hook sizes to suit the bait and target. Best For: Fast re-rigging without losing fishing time, and for anglers who prefer choosing their own hook sizes. Targets: Whatever you rig it for — from reef bruisers like trout and red emperor to pelagics and everything in between. Recommended Use: Pair with your preferred hooks (J or circle), add bait, and drop straight in. Available in 80lb or 100lb mono for serious stopping power. Pack Contents: 3× pre-tied blanks per pack. Keep a pack handy to save time if your leader gets damaged or sharked! Match your hook size to bait profile — small squid and pilchards = smaller hooks, slabs and whole fish = larger hooks. Pre-rig your hooks on spare blanks at home for instant changeovers on the water.

sections.heading: Slayers on the Reef
sections.text: In July 2025, we took the Swains Slayer Series™ to one of Australia’s toughest fishing grounds. From stunning sunsets to hard-fighting reef fish, this trip proved what these rigs were made for — creating unforgettable memories on the reef. Swains Reef is one of Australia’s most demanding reef environments, combining coral structure, strong current and aggressive fish species. These rigs are designed for situations where standard surf or estuary rigs are quickly damaged or outmatched

sections.heading: Rig Care & Maintenance
sections.text: Keep Your Slayers Fighting Fit Your Swains Slayer rigs are built tough — hand tied right here in Australia using only the best gear. Look after them properly, and they’ll outlast the cheap imports every time. Here’s how to keep them in top shape:

sections.heading: 1. Rinse After Every Session
sections.text: Saltwater is brutal. After each trip, give your rigs a rinse in fresh water. A quick bucket dunk or a spray with the hose knocks out the salt crystals that chew through line and hardware. Don’t just stuff them back in the tackle box wet. Lay them on a towel, hang them in the shade, or give them a bit of airflow. Avoid direct sun — UV cooks line faster than a barra on a barbie. Keep your rigs organised in resealable bags, rig wallets, or foam winders. Burying hooks in foam stops tangles and protects the points. Label them by species or rig type so you can grab and go when the bite’s on. (If you open the original rig packet at the bottom, you can reseal it)

sections.heading: 4. Inspect Before Re-Use
sections.text: Before tying one on again, check the leader for nicks, worn knots, or chafing. Touch up dull hooks with a file, and swap out any floats, beads, or skirts that have lost their flash. A sharp rig equals a hooked fish. Don’t abandon your rigs in a hot car or leave them baking on the deck. Store them cool, dry, and out of direct sunlight. Toss a silica pack in your rig wallet if you’re stashing them long-term. “Treat your Slayer rig like a good deckie — rinse it, dry it, and don’t throw it in a rusty bucket. Do that, and it’ll keep slaying long after the cheap imports and copycat knockoffs have curled up and died.”

sections.heading: Match the Amount of Flash to the Conditions
sections.text: A flasher rig places reflective material beside the hook and bait, helping fish notice it as the fibres move and catch the available light. Flasher rigs are particularly useful when: • Breaking surf and whitewater reduce visibility • Sand, current or runoff has stirred the water • Fishing around dawn, dusk or under overcast skies • Fishing deeper water where less natural light reaches the bait • Fish are moving quickly through the area and have limited time to find the bait As visibility improves, reduce the amount of flash. A lightly dressed flasher can provide enough movement and contrast in clear water without overpowering the natural bait. The aim is not to use the brightest rig available. It is to make the bait easier to locate while keeping the amount of flash appropriate for the water clarity, available light and behaviour of the fish. This guide explains how those conditions affect flasher choice and when a standard bait rig may be the better option.

sections.heading: How Flasher Material Helps Fish Find the Bait
sections.text: Flasher material does not produce its own light. It reflects the available light as the fibres move with the current, creating brief changes in brightness, colour and contrast beside the hook. This movement can help fish: • Notice the hook and bait against the surrounding water • Locate the bait more quickly in reduced visibility • Track the bait as it moves in current • Focus their strike close to the hook The flasher works alongside the bait rather than replacing it. The reflective fibres provide the visual cue, while the natural bait supplies scent and something for the fish to eat. Positioning the flash close to the hook concentrates that colour and movement where the fish needs to strike. This is particularly useful when fish are moving through the area quickly or only have a brief opportunity to inspect the bait.

sections.heading: How Water Clarity Changes Flasher Choice
sections.text: Water clarity determines how easily fish can see the bait and how much additional flash is useful. Fish can inspect the bait from farther away. Use a lightly dressed flasher that adds subtle movement and reflection without dominating the natural bait. Slightly Coloured Water A moderate amount of flash helps the bait remain visible as suspended sand, runoff or stirred sediment reduces visibility. This is where many general-purpose flasher rigs work particularly well. Whitewater or Dirty Water Breaking surf and heavily stirred water give fish less time and distance to locate the bait. Brighter colours, stronger contrast and a larger amount of reflective material can make the bait easier to find. Water clarity can change with tide, wind, rainfall and wave action. Match the flasher to the water being fished rather than automatically using the same colour and amount of flash on every trip.

sections.heading: Choose the Flasher Hook, Rig Layout and Strength Separately
sections.text: Choosing a flasher rig involves more than selecting its colour. The hook, leader and rig layout must also suit the bait, target fish and ground being fished. Use an individual hand-tied flasher hook when you already have a suitable rig and want to add flash close to the bait. Use a flasher paternoster rig from beaches, rock platforms or boats when the bait needs to be held above the seabed with the flash positioned close to the hooks. From the beach, it keeps the baits visible in surf wash and moving water. From a boat, it provides control when lowering baits onto reef or into deeper water. Use a heavier flasher paternoster when fishing deeper water, stronger current or hard reef where larger fish must be kept away from structure. Whichever layout is used: • Match the hook size to the bait • Match the leader strength to the fish and ground • Match the amount of flash to the water clarity and available light • Keep the bait and hook point clear of excessive flasher material The flash attracts attention, but the hook, leader and complete rig still need to be appropriate for the fishing conditions.

sections.heading: Choosing a Wiggle ya Worm Flasher Option
sections.text: The available flasher options cover three different uses: • Individual Hi-Viz flasher hooks for adding colour and movement to an existing rig • 60lb flasher paternoster rigs for general reef, offshore and mixed-species fishing • 80lb flasher paternoster rigs for deeper water, heavier tackle and larger reef species Choose the individual hook when you already have a suitable rig. Choose a complete paternoster when you need the sinker, backbone and paternoster arms to control the complete setup. The three options are explained below.

sections.heading: Premium Hand-Tied Hi-Viz Fishing Flashers
sections.text: These are individual 6/0 or 8/0 beak hooks dressed with long, high-visibility flasher material rather than complete fishing rigs. The dressing is significantly larger and fuller than a standard flasher, producing more colour, reflection and movement around the hook. Use these when you want a pronounced visual target rather than the subtle flash provided by a lightly dressed hook. They suit fishos who want to add a flasher hook to their own leader or rig while selecting the leader strength, sinker arrangement and complete rig layout separately. Add a small piece of natural bait to provide scent while leaving the hook point and gape exposed. Choose the 6/0 hook for smaller baits and the 8/0 hook when using a larger bait or targeting larger fish. Best suited to: Building or modifying bait rigs where strong colour, movement and visibility are required.

sections.heading: 60lb Kingfish & Snapper Twisted Flasher Paternoster Rig
sections.text: This complete paternoster rig uses a 60lb monofilament backbone with twin 6/0 recurve circle hooks positioned on twisted paternoster arms. The sinker attaches at the bottom of the rig, allowing the baited flasher hooks to fish above the reef or seabed. The twisted arms help hold the hooks away from the backbone while the flasher material places colour and movement directly beside each bait. The 60lb construction provides a practical balance for general reef and offshore fishing without stepping up to the heavier 80lb flasher rig. Best suited to: Snapper, kingfish and mixed reef species around general reef, offshore ground and deeper inshore water.

sections.heading: 80lb Snapper Flasher Double Paternoster Rig
sections.text: This heavier flasher paternoster uses an 80lb monofilament backbone with twin 10/0 sport circle hooks for larger baits and powerful reef species. The hooks are positioned above the bottom sinker, keeping both baited flashers fishing close to the reef while the paternoster layout provides control in deeper water and stronger current. The heavier leader, larger hooks and double-hook layout suit situations where the 60lb rig does not provide enough strength or hook size for the bait and fish being targeted. Best suited to: Deeper offshore reefs, hard structure and larger species including red emperor, nannygai, coral trout and snapper.

sections.heading: Best Fishing Rigs in Australia (2026 Fisho Guide)
sections.text: Choosing the right fishing rig can make the difference between a quiet session and one you'll remember. In Australian waters, where species, conditions and fishing environments vary enormously, there is no single rig that works everywhere. This guide explains the fishing rigs that consistently work across Australian beaches, estuaries, rock platforms and offshore reefs, when each one performs best, and links to detailed guides that help you choose the right setup for your fishing. Whether you're new to fishing or looking to improve your results, understanding which rig suits your target species and the conditions you're fishing is one of the fastest ways to catch more fish.

sections.heading: How to Choose the Right Fishing Rig
sections.text: Most fishos overthink choosing a fishing rig. In reality, it usually comes down to answering three simple questions: • What species are you targeting? • Where are you fishing? (Beach, estuary, rock platform, reef or offshore.) • What bait are you using? The size and type of bait often influences which rig will present it most naturally and keep it fishing effectively. We'll explain this in more detail later in the guide when we look at the strengths of each rig type. Once you've answered those three questions, choosing the right rig becomes much easier. If you're still unsure which rig best suits your fishing, use the Australian Fishing Rig Decision Guide for step-by-step recommendations or try the Rig Finder for a personalised recommendation based on where you're fishing and what you're targeting. If you'd like to understand why different rig designs behave differently underwater before choosing one, read Understanding Fishing Rigs: The Foundation of Successful Fishing .

sections.heading: Choose Your Rig Around the Species You're Targeting
sections.text: The species you're targeting is one of the best places to start when choosing a fishing rig. Different fish feed in different ways, live in different environments and often require different bait presentations. Whiting and bream generally respond best to naturally presented baits fished close to the sand. Snapper and mulloway often require stronger leaders and larger hooks to handle bigger baits and powerful runs. Kingfish are commonly targeted using live baits or large strip baits fished close to structure, while sharks and other powerful predators require heavy-duty rigs designed to handle extreme pressure and abrasion. It's important to remember that choosing a species is only the first step. The same fish can often be caught using different rigs depending on where you're fishing, the conditions on the day and the type of bait you're using. If you already know the species you're targeting, these dedicated Australian guides will help you choose the right rig: • Best Whiting Rigs in Australia • Best Bream Rigs in Australia • Best Flathead Rigs in Australia • Best Tailor Rigs in Australia • Best Australian Salmon Rigs • Best Snapper Rigs in Australia • Best Mulloway Rigs in Australia • Best Kingfish Rigs in Australia • Best Gummy Shark Rigs in Australia • Best Shark Rigs in Australia

sections.heading: Where You’re Fishing Changes Everything
sections.text: The same bait behaves very differently depending on location. Beach fishing rewards streamlined rigs that cast cleanly and resist tangles in surf. Estuary rigs prioritise finesse and natural drift. Reef fishing demands stronger leaders and controlled bait positioning near structure. For leader strength, rig spacing and sinker selection around coral and bommies, see the Best Reef Fishing Rigs in Australia guide → Understanding beach structure alone can dramatically improve rig selection before you even cast. See How to Read a Beach: Spotting Gutters, Banks & Breaks Like a Pro . Fishing after dark also changes how predators approach bait. Learn how timing affects rig choice in Night Beach Fishing Tips .

sections.heading: Casting Distance vs Presentation
sections.text: Some rigs are built to fly. Others are built to fish. Long cast pulley rigs protect bait during the cast and deploy cleanly on splashdown, making them ideal when fish are holding beyond the breakers. Paternoster rigs may not cast as far, but they present bait cleanly and reliably in close gutters and changing surf. To see exactly how pulley rigs achieve both distance and clean presentation, read How Long Cast Pulley Rigs Really Work .

sections.heading: Hook Style Actually Matters
sections.text: Hook choice affects hook-up success more than most fishos realise. Circle hooks improve corner-of-mouth hook placement on larger species. J-style hooks suit active bait fishing. Sliding snelled twin-hook rigs improve presentation when fishing whole squid or large slab baits. If you want a practical breakdown of how hook choice changes rig performance, see Choosing the Right Fishing Hook (Why Most Fishos Get It Wrong) .

sections.heading: Strength vs Fishability
sections.text: Heavier isn’t always better. Increasing leader strength helps around reef and toothy fish, but going too heavy can reduce bait movement and bites in calm water. Offshore structure fishing has its own balance between abrasion resistance and presentation. The goal is simple: enough strength to land the fish without reducing presentation quality Modern modular systems also allow fishos to quickly scale trace strength, hook size, and bait presentation without changing the entire backbone rig setup. Small adjustments like bead colour and contrast can also improve visibility in moving water. See Using Colour and Contrast in Rigs to Trigger More Bites .

sections.heading: Best Fishing Rigs by Type (Real-World Proven)
sections.text: There are hundreds of rig variations used around Australia, but only a handful consistently perform across environments.

sections.heading: Everyday Beach Rigs (Simple, Effective, Reliable)

sections.heading: All-Rounder Predator Rigs (Versatile and Proven)
sections.text: Twin-hook rigs with adjustable spacing handle larger baits across beaches, estuaries and reef edges and are commonly used when targeting structure-holding predators like kingfish with live or slab baits. See the Kingfish Rig Guide → Snapper & Mulloway Twin Hook Rig Estuary Mulloway Twin Hook Rig Fishing specifically for mulloway? See our Beach Mulloway guide →

sections.heading: Long Cast Beach Rigs (When Distance Matters)
sections.text: Pulley rigs streamline your bait during the cast and deploy cleanly on splashdown, improving both range and presentation. See How Long Cast Pulley Rigs Really Work → Proven Example: Long Cast Beach Pulley Rig More adaptable modular long cast systems now also allow fishos to quickly swap trace styles, bait presentations, and specialised setups without rebuilding complete rigs between sessions or changing surf conditions. sections.heading: Heavy-Duty Predator Rigs (For Serious Fish)
sections.text: Heavy coated wire rigs are essential when targeting sharks and toothy predators in demanding surf environments. 650lb Coated Wire Shark Rig For lighter surf sharks, see our gummy shark rigs guide →

sections.heading: Offshore & Reef Rigs (Strength Over Structure)
sections.text: Twisted paternoster rigs remain one of the most reliable offshore setups because they resist tangles and keep bait positioned just above reef structure. Offshore Reef Twisted Paternoster Fishing coral structure or targeting trout, emperor and reef predators? See the Best Reef Fishing Rigs in Australia guide →

sections.heading: Hand-Tied vs Store-Bought Rigs
sections.text: Mass-produced rigs often work fine in calm water, but Australian fishing regularly involves heavy surf, reef abrasion and powerful fish. Hand-tied rigs allow better control over: hook placement leader strength connection reliability component quality That’s why experienced fishos often move toward purpose-built rigs over time.

sections.heading: Common Rig Mistakes Fishos Make
sections.text: Using the same rig everywhere is one of the most common problems. Other mistakes include: overbuilding rigs for calm conditions underbuilding rigs near structure ignoring current strength using mismatched hook sizes Avoiding these issues alone improves results quickly. See Common Fishing Rig Mistakes (And How to Fix Them) .

sections.heading: Our Top Rig Picks (Real-World Favourites)
sections.text: If you're building a dependable rig kit, a few proven rig styles cover most situations: Twin-hook predator rigs for versatility Double paternoster rigs for everyday beach fishing Long cast pulley rigs for distance Twisted paternosters for offshore durability Heavy shark rigs for extreme conditions These rig styles have stood the test of time because they consistently work in Australian waters. If you'd like a quick rig recommendation based on where and what you're fishing, try the Rig Finder.

sections.heading: Bringing It All Together
sections.text: Choosing the right fishing rig doesn’t need to be complicated. More advanced systems now also allow fishos to adapt rigs faster as conditions change. Modular long cast systems can help reduce downtime on the beach by allowing interchangeable trace setups designed for different species, bait sizes, surf conditions, and fishing environments. sections.heading: Australian Fishing Rig Finder
sections.text: Not every fishing rig works in every situation. The Wiggle ya Worm Rig Finder helps match fishing rigs to your target species, fishing environment, bait choice, tidal current and casting distance using practical Australian fishing knowledge developed through years of real-world experience. Instead of scrolling through hundreds of rigs, the Rig Finder narrows down the most suitable options based on the conditions you actually fish. Designed for Australian surf, estuary, offshore reef and land-based shark fishing conditions. Select the details you know about your fishing conditions. The more information you provide, the more accurately the Rig Finder can recommend suitable rigs. The Rig Finder considers factors including: • Fishing environment • Casting distance It then recommends up to three rigs best suited to your fishing conditions, explains why they're recommended, suggests suitable sinker setups, and links to setup guides where available.

sections.heading: Built Around Real Australian Fishing Conditions
sections.text: The Wiggle ya Worm Rig Finder is built on practical Australian fishing knowledge developed through years of fishing, testing and refining rigs across a wide range of conditions. Rather than offering generic tackle advice or endless product lists, the Rig Finder recommends the rigs most suited to your target species, fishing environment and fishing conditions. Each recommendation is supported by practical setup advice, sinker suggestions and links to detailed rig guides where available, helping you understand not only which rig to use, but why it suits the conditions. The recommendation system continues to evolve as new fishing knowledge, techniques and proven rig designs are added.

sections.heading: Fishing with a Drone?
sections.text: The Rig Finder has been developed to recommend proven rigs for conventional Australian surf, estuary, reef and land-based shark fishing.
